text.p: The leader of one of Colombia's right-wing death squads was expelled on Wednesday from a nationwide paramilitary alliance because of links with drug trafficking.

The move, announced in a communique from the so-called "United Peasant Self-Defense Groups of Colombia" (AUC), came less than a week after anti-drugs police discovered four drug laboratories said to be operated by one of the outlawed paramilitary gangs in central Cundinamarca province.

"We found out about the discovery of the laboratory in Yacopi and asked Commander Byron to admit responsibility ... given his refusal to do so we have decided to exclude him from our national movement," said the communique, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.

Commander Byron, whose real name is not known, is a regional death squad chieftain whose forces operate in the central Magdalena Medio region -- home to the country's first illegal paramilitary forces in the early 1980s.
The decision to oust him from the alliance is the first public example of the clandestine paramilitary group's bid to distance itself from accusations that it is linked to the drug trade.
The alliance was set up in April at a secret summit between the leaders of all the country's main death squads, which are fighting against leftist guerrillas and their suspected sympathizers.
